title: Database Fundamentals
summary: A database is a managed collection of data with a query language, integrity rules, and a storage engine.

title: Relational Databases
summary: Data as relations (tables), queried with algebra/calculus, constrained by keys.

title: SQL
summary: The declarative language of relational databases: SELECT describes the result, not the plan.

title: Tables
summary: Named relations: a heading of columns and a body of rows. Duplicates depend on whether you mean bag or set.

title: Primary Keys
summary: A column (or set) that uniquely identifies a row. The handle the rest of the schema points at.

title: Foreign Keys
summary: A column that must match a key in another table. Referential integrity as a constraint, not a hope.

title: Constraints
summary: Declarations the engine enforces: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FK — integrity that survives a bad insert.

title: Joins
summary: Combining rows from two relations by a predicate: inner, left, right, full, cross, and the nested-loop vs hash implementations.

title: Aggregation
summary: GROUP BY, HAVING, and the reduction of many rows to a statistic.

title: Subqueries
summary: A query used as a value, a table, or a predicate. Correlated vs uncorrelated is the performance fork.

title: Indexes
summary: Auxiliary structures (usually B+ trees) that make predicates cheap at the cost of writes and space.

title: Views
summary: Named queries. Virtual by default; materialized when you cache the result.

title: Transactions
summary: A grouping of reads and writes that should succeed or fail as a unit.

title: ACID
summary: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the classical transaction contract.

title: Isolation Levels
summary: Read uncommitted through serializable: which anomalies you tolerate for concurrency.

title: Locks (DB)
summary: Shared/exclusive, row/table, intention locks. Two-phase locking as a correctness argument.

title: MVCC
summary: Readers see a snapshot; writers create versions. Postgres and InnoDB's answer to blocking reads.

title: Database Concurrency
summary: Interleaving transactions without losing integrity. Conflict serializability is the theory.

title: Normalization
summary: Decomposing schemas to remove redundancy. Normal forms are tests, not decorations.

title: 1NF
summary: Atomic values in cells; no repeating groups. The floor of the relational model.

title: 2NF
summary: 1NF plus no partial dependence of a non-key attribute on part of a composite key.

title: 3NF
summary: 2NF plus no transitive dependence of a non-key attribute on the key.

title: BCNF
summary: Every determinant is a candidate key. Stricter than 3NF; sometimes you lose a dependency.

title: Query Optimization
summary: Turning SQL into a cheap plan: statistics, join order, and access paths.

title: Query Planners
summary: Cost-based vs rule-based planners, EXPLAIN, and why the optimizer is the real engine.

title: Storage Engines
summary: The physical implementation: heap files, clustered indexes, InnoDB vs MyISAM vs LSM.

title: Buffer Pool
summary: The database's cache of disk pages. Replacement policy, dirty pages, and checkpoints.

title: Write-Ahead Log
summary: Log the change before the page. Redo/undo, crash recovery, and replication's raw feed.

title: B-Trees
summary: Balanced multiway trees. Internal nodes hold keys and children; used widely in filesystems and DBs.

title: B+ Trees
summary: All values in leaves, leaves linked. The index structure behind almost every relational PK.

title: Replication (DB)
summary: Copying data to other nodes: statement vs row, sync vs async, failover.

title: Sharding
summary: Partitioning rows across machines by a key. Hotspots and resharding are the cost.

title: Partitioning
summary: Splitting a table by range, list, or hash — within one instance or across them.

title: Key-Value Stores
summary: The simplest NoSQL: get/put by key. Redis, Dynamo-style systems.

title: Document Stores
summary: JSON/BSON documents with secondary indexes. Schema-on-read, query-on-fields.

title: Column Stores
summary: Values stored by column, not row. Analytics, compression, and vectorized execution.

title: Graph Databases
summary: First-class nodes and edges. Index-free adjacency and graph query languages.

title: Wi-Fi
summary: 802.11: association, airtime, and a MAC that is nothing like a switched Ethernet.

title: BGP
summary: The internet's inter-domain routing protocol: path vectors, policy, and the default-free zone.

title: OSPF
summary: A link-state IGP: flood LSAs, run Dijkstra, install routes in the RIB.

title: Spanning Tree
summary: A loop-free active topology on a switched LAN. Without it, broadcasts amplify until the LAN dies.

title: fork()
summary: Copy a process: the child gets 0, the parent gets a pid. Copy-on-write makes the copy cheap until a write.

title: Working Set
summary: The pages a process is actually using. If they do not fit in RAM, the system thrashes.

title: What is Programming?
summary: Writing precise instructions a machine can execute, and choosing the data those instructions work on.

title: Variables
summary: A name bound to a value in memory. Assignment rebinds or overwrites; scope decides where the name is visible.

title: Data Types
summary: The kind of value: integers, floats, booleans, text, and collections. The type decides the operations, the memory, and the pitfalls.

title: Conditionals
summary: Branching: run one path or another based on a Boolean expression. The first decision a program can make.

title: Loops
summary: Repeat work while a condition holds or for each item in a collection. The source of both power and infinite loops.

title: Functions
summary: A named, reusable computation with inputs (parameters) and an output (return value). The unit of abstraction and of testing.

title: Recursion
summary: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller piece. It needs a base case and progress toward it.

title: Stack and Heap
summary: Where a running program keeps its data: the fast, automatic call stack and the flexible, longer-lived heap.

title: Pointers and References
summary: A value that is a memory address. Pointers let code share, modify, and link data without copying it.

title: Error Handling
summary: Deciding what a program does when something goes wrong: raise, return, retry, or stop — and always clean up.

title: Testing and Debugging
summary: Checking behavior against expectations, and finding why it differs. Reproduce, hypothesize, observe, fix, lock in with a test.

title: Compiled vs Interpreted
summary: How source text becomes behavior: translated ahead of time, executed by a program, or both. A property of implementations, not languages.

title: Type Systems
summary: The rules a language uses to classify values and reject nonsense: static or dynamic, nominal or structural, with or without inference.

title: Garbage Collection
summary: Automatic memory management: the runtime finds objects nothing can reach any more and reclaims them.

title: Python
summary: A readable, dynamically typed, batteries-included language. Fast to write, slower to run, dominant for scripting, data, and glue.

title: C
summary: A small, compiled language close to the hardware. Manual memory, pointers, and no safety net — the language operating systems are written in.

title: C++
summary: C plus abstractions with no run-time tax: classes, templates, and RAII. Powerful and large.

title: Java
summary: A statically typed, class-based language that compiles to bytecode for the JVM. Portable, safe, and everywhere in back ends.

title: JavaScript
summary: The language of the browser and, through Node.js, of servers. Dynamic, function-first, and single-threaded on an event loop.

title: TypeScript
summary: JavaScript with a static type system on top. The checker runs at build time and the types are erased before the code runs.

title: Classes and Objects
summary: A class is a blueprint that bundles data with the operations on it; an object is one instance with its own state.

title: Encapsulation
summary: Hide an object's state behind a small interface so it can protect its own invariants.

title: Abstraction and Interfaces
summary: Depend on what something does, not how it does it. Interfaces name the behavior and hide the implementation.

title: Inheritance
summary: A subclass reuses and extends a superclass. It models 'is-a' relationships — and creates the tightest coupling in OOP.

title: Polymorphism
summary: One call, many behaviors: the actual method that runs depends on the object's type at run time.

title: Composition vs Inheritance
summary: Build behavior by combining objects (has-a) rather than extending classes (is-a). It is looser, more flexible, and easier to change.

title: SOLID Principles
summary: Five heuristics for object-oriented design that keep code easy to change: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov, interface segregation, dependency inversion.

title: Design Patterns
summary: Named, reusable solutions to recurring design problems: creational, structural, and behavioral.

title: Big-O and Complexity
summary: How an algorithm's cost grows with input size, ignoring constants. The language for comparing solutions before you run them.

title: Arrays
summary: A contiguous block of same-sized elements. Constant-time indexing, cache-friendly scans, and costly middle inserts.

title: Linked Lists
summary: Nodes that each hold a value and a pointer to the next. Cheap splicing, no random access.

title: Stacks
summary: Last in, first out. Push and pop at one end in constant time — the structure behind calls, undo, and depth-first search.

title: Queues
summary: First in, first out. Enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front — the shape of fairness, buffers, and breadth-first search.

title: Hash Tables
summary: Turn a key into an array index with a hash function. Average constant-time lookup, insert, and delete.

title: Sorting
summary: Arrange items in order. Comparison sorts cannot beat O(n log n); merge sort and quicksort get there by dividing the problem.

title: Binary Search
summary: Halve a sorted search space each step. O(log n) lookups — and a template for searching on any monotonic condition.

title: Binary Search Trees
summary: A tree where left descendants are smaller and right descendants are larger. Ordered data with O(log n) operations — when balanced.

title: Heaps and Priority Queues
summary: A tree stored in an array where every parent is smaller (min-heap) than its children. Constant-time min and logarithmic push/pop.

title: Tries
summary: A tree keyed by characters or bits that shares prefixes. Prefix search and longest-prefix match in time proportional to the key length.

title: Graphs
summary: Vertices connected by edges. The general model for networks, maps, dependencies, and relationships.

title: Breadth-First Search
summary: Explore a graph level by level using a queue. Finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

title: Depth-First Search
summary: Follow one path as far as it goes, then backtrack. The basis for cycle detection, topological sort, and exhaustive search.

title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
summary: Shortest paths from one vertex in a graph with non-negative weights, by repeatedly settling the closest unsettled vertex.

title: Dynamic Programming
summary: Solve a problem by combining solutions to overlapping subproblems, computed once each. Recursion plus a table.
